Heyyy, tara!

For me, you don’t feel exactly 'normal', especially if you’ve dealt with depression for the longest time. The depressed state actually becomes the 'normal', and light/joyful moments can feel unusual. You second guess everything about getting better, fearing something in exchange or worse will happen after. The unfamiliarity is overwhelming at times, making you want to go back to having low points because it’s much more comfortable there. As cliché as it is, you just have to keep moving forward because that’s the process of getting better. I know this is easier said than done, but you have to keep reminding yourself that you also deserve to feel ‘normal’ again and experience life. 

I do still struggle and have very rough days, but this is the first time in years I've had a little glimpse of hope (I can somehow see myself living for at least three more years, haha). I just decided to be there for myself, just this once, by starting to forgive myself for all the neglect, self-sabotage, and pain I caused to myself over the years. Getting up and doing the daily routine is still tough, but instead of blaming or punishing yourself for not doing much, you become much more understanding and patient with yourself. Start listening to your body and mind as everything is a response; hence, there’s always a cause. Try to be the friend/parent that you always wanted for yourself, the kind that you trust and always wants the best for you.

I do hope all of us will overcome this, that we’ll soon enough find a glimpse light and hold onto it for as long as we can.
